/notes/http-caching.body:
Field Notes

HTTP caching in five headers

Cache-Control: max-age=N says a response stays fresh for N seconds. Until then a cache may reuse it without asking the server.

Cache-Control: no-cache does not mean "do not cache". A cache may store the response but must check with the server before reusing it.

Cache-Control: no-store is the one that means "do not keep a copy at all".

Cache-Control: private allows the browser's own cache but not shared caches such as a CDN.

ETag gives a response a version tag. The client sends it back in If-None-Match; if nothing changed, the server answers 304 Not Modified with no body.

/privacy.body:
Field Notes

Privacy notice

This site is part of a research project on automated web traffic, including AI agents.

What is recorded. For every request: the time, IP address, the address requested, all request headers (including the browser or program name it reports), any data sent, and connection details such as the TLS version. A small script on each page reports whether scripts ran and whether the page was scrolled, the pointer moved or a key pressed. It does not read or store anything on your device. No cookies are set.

Why. To measure how people, ordinary bots and AI agents differ in the requests they make.

How long. Raw logs are kept until 31 January 2027 and then deleted. Anything published will have IP addresses removed, except addresses on AI companies' published crawler lists.

Contact. CONTACT-EMAIL-NOT-SET, for questions or to ask for records of your IP address to be deleted.
